summary: Ephemeral CI runner SSH tunnel teardown during secret rotation prevented artifact publish to internal registry
description:
Issue summary:
During the overnight release window on 2026-03-10 we observed a wave of failed artifact publish jobs originating from ephemeral CI runners. Failures started at ~02:12 UTC and affected three concurrent release jobs that push container images to our internal registry.

Impact:
- 3 release pipelines blocked (nightly and two hotfix pipelines).
- Artifact push errors showed as connection resets and failed SSH multiplex sessions to the registry bastion.
- No customer-facing services were impacted, but release doors remained closed until manual intervention.

Observed behaviour:
- Runners reported SSH connection closed/EOF immediately after Vault transit rewrap requests completed.
- CI job logs show "ssh_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host" and subsequent "failed to upload artifact: unexpected EOF".

Why this is a support ticket (internal):
- The sequence appears tied to a coordinated key rotation (Vault transit re-wrap) that ran across secrets-manager and our SSH bastion bootstrap script. We need release engineering + infra to validate runner credential handoff and avoid disruption in future rotations.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger ephemeral runner to start a long-running job that opens a persistent SSH multiplex to registry bastion (ControlMaster enabled).
2) Initiate a Vault transit rewrap/rekey for the SSH host keys/runner signing keys.
3) Observe the runner's ssh multiplex connection drop and subsequent SCP/docker push errors when the agent tries to reuse the socket.

Note: This was reproduced in a private staging replay by running the same rewrap on a single region agent; the timing window is narrow and tied to long-running multiplexed connections.
logs:
Excerpt from runner (runner-ephemeral-92) at 2026-03-10T02:12:15Z:
[2026-03-10T02:12:15Z] ssh_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
[2026-03-10T02:12:15Z] ERROR: failed to upload artifact: unexpected EOF
Vault operator logs during same window:
[2026-03-10T02:12:12Z] transit.rewrap: key_id=projects/global/keys/runner-ssh rewrap started
[2026-03-10T02:12:14Z] transit.rewrap: key_id=projects/global/keys/runner-ssh rewrap completed
Proxy (bastion) syslog:
Mar 10 02:12:13 bastion-7 sshd[22418]: Received SIGHUP from 1; reloading host keys
Mar 10 02:12:15 bastion-7 sshd[22418]: Terminated control master for user=ci-runner pid=21999
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Vault rewrap triggered a host-key swap (or restart) on the SSH bastion which caused active ControlMaster connections to be torn down. Runners using ControlPersist/ControlMaster expect persistent sockets; when the server restarts or reloads host keys, server will close existing connections, leaving client sockets in an inconsistent state.

What we checked:
- Confirmed Vault transit rewrap job ran at the same time as failures (logs above).
- Verified bastion restarted sshd (SIGHUP/host-key reload) during the window.
- Replayed sequence in staging by forcing sshd reload and observed identical ControlMaster teardown symptoms.
- Confirmed ephemeral runners do not currently have a post-restart socket validation step; they attempt to reuse the socket which leads to immediate EOF on reuse.

Open questions:
- Why did the rewrap trigger an sshd reload on bastion instead of a hot-swap without connection terminations? (Configuration in ansible playbook triggers sshd -H reload path).
- Is our runner bootstrap able to detect socket death and reconnect gracefully under the current retry policy?

Preliminary root cause (working): "Vault transit rewrap triggered sshd host-key reload on bastion hosts, which closed active SSH multiplex sockets; ephemeral runner clients attempted to reuse dead ControlMaster sockets without reconnecting, causing artifact upload failures."
workaround:
Short-term mitigation applied 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC:
- Support/Release Eng performed manual restart of blocked jobs using fresh runner instances (control socket recreated).
- Ops adjusted the rotation job to stagger across bastion nodes to avoid simultaneous restart of all sshd instances.

Tactical steps for immediate next release window:
- Disable ControlPersist reuse in the release runner job templates (set -o ControlMaster=no) for critical publishes until fix is in place.
- Add runner retry that validates connection with a lightweight 'ssh -O check' before attempting publish.
next_steps:
1) Infra to change bastion rotation playbook to use host-key hot-swap path that preserves existing sessions where possible, or stagger restarts across nodes (owner: Priya Shah).
2) CI/Release Eng to add idempotent socket health-check and reconnection logic to ephemeral runner bootstrap and push scripts (owner: Marcus Li).
3) Patch release template to disable ControlMaster reuse for critical artifact publishes and roll this change across release pipelines (owner: Release Eng).
4) Add an automated test in staging that runs a simulated rewrap during long-running job to detect regressions (owner: QA).

Target timeline: mitigations deployed to staging within 3 days; production rotation policy updated before the next scheduled key rotation cycle.
root_cause: Active SSH multiplex sessions were closed by the bastion sshd reload initiated as part of a key rewrap; client-side logic attempted socket reuse without verifying liveness, causing immediate EOFs during artifact push.
